I Found Vietnam’s Best Bowl of Pho… Down an Alley You’d Walk Right Past
Nov 2025 • Solo
Pho Minh sits tucked down a quiet little alley off Pasteur, a spot you’d miss if you weren’t looking for it. They’ve been serving pho here since 1945, and you can feel that history the moment you walk in. The atmosphere is calm and unpretentious, a welcome pause from the pace of the city, and exactly the kind of place where great food quietly happens.

The food lives up to its reputation, and then some. The broth is the star — rich, fragrant, and layered with the kind of depth that only decades of craft can produce. One sip and you understand why Pho Minh has earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand. The beef is tender and fresh, the herbs vibrant, and everything lands in perfect balance. It’s pho with soul.

Service is warm, efficient, and genuinely welcoming. This is a family-run shop, and it shows in the small touches — a smile at the door, bowls arriving quickly, and a steady rhythm in the kitchen that only experience creates.

Value is exceptional. For a restaurant recognised by Michelin and boasting nearly 80 years of history, the pricing is incredibly modest for the quality you get. Easily one of the best meals of the trip without straining the budget.

Wait time has never been an issue for us. Even when busy, the operation is smooth and fast, and steaming bowls arrive in minutes.

Overall, Pho Minh became a standout highlight of our Vietnam trip. A humble alleyway, a historic kitchen, and a bowl of pho that sets the benchmark. If you’re looking for something truly authentic in Ho Chi Minh City, this is the place.

Insider tip:
Go early. Pho Minh shines in the morning when the broth is at its absolute best and the shop is calm. Anytime before 10am is ideal.

I left sated and happy
Apr 2024 • Solo
6:30am. First customer of the day, they were still pushing their bikes out as I took my seat. I had allowed extra time to reach this restaurant as it has a notorious reputation of being hard to find as it is located at the end of a long and narrow alley. The restaurant ebbed and flowed as I enjoyed a pate chaud starter followed by a bowl of delicious phở tái. There were plenty of accompaniments, super fresh Thai basil, Ngò Gai (sawtooth) & mint, which is far less common, but I found the mint added a great freshness to the already most excellent broth. There were also lime wedges, a plenty, endless raw sliced chilli, and lightly blanched bean sprouts. Some items that I didn't need on this occasion, hoisin & sriracha sauces. The other customers were exclusively Vietnamese, ether businessmen, or whole families with children of various ages. They came and went as I ate at a relaxed pace. The noodles were perfectly cooked, and the broth needed very little adjustment to hit the spot, just the juice of three lime wedges, a generous amount of chopped chillies, and the aforementioned mint leaves. For me, pho is not complete without Thai basil, and today's herbs were really fresh and vibrant. Some tables had been used three times over in the forty minutes I took to savour my breakfast. This restaurant has something of a cult following, and now I know why. They keep very limited hours, opening at 6:30am and closing three and a half hours later at 10 am. The food is prepared in a room on the other side of the alley, where there were some spill over tables and seats. Everything was spotlessly clean and efficiently run it is immediately obvious that they let the food do the talking for them, and I am happy to report it speaks volumes. This is my 21st bowl of pho for my 30 in 30-days challenge, and it easily jumped into 2nd best place, so it was a great find. I am a happy man, a very happy and sated man. Cost wise, I found it very reasonable, not cheap, not expensive, so no quibbles there.

We ate here every day for breakfast
Nov 2019
There's no menu but why would you need one? On our first day, we sat at a table, indicated "two" and that's all that was needed to order. A plate piled high with fragrant fresh herbs and a dish with banh pate chaud (a meat-filled pastry) were set on the table, followed a few minutes later by steaming bowls of excellent pho bo. 

Taste the broth before adding any lime juice, chilis, herbs, etc - it's amazing! The "standard" bowl of pho bo will have slices of tender, still-pink beef that will "cook" in the hot soup. But by the second day, I managed to order my favorite kind: pho gun bo (beef tendon). Or try asking for pho dac biet (special) which might include a bit of all the cuts they have available. 

Regardless of what you get, it's all delicious! They're open by 6:30am so get there early and get your day started in the most delicious way.

Hidden gem
Jul 2019 • Solo
After having read a few convincing reviews about this restaurant, I decided to try it out myself. Not easy to find the place. It is located in a small alley in Pasteur. Walking up Pasteur (in the direction of the traffic), the alley is on your left hand side right next to Liberty Central.
Eating at Pho Minh feels like you are eating where locals do! The restaurant setup was expectedly very basic and the place was filled by Vietnamese people.
I ordered a Pho, two beef buns (see photo) and a Viet coffee with condensed milk. The waiters were very kind and everything was delicious. The bill was 109,000 VTD (~4.68 USD).
Give it a try and you won’t regret it! :)
